title: Elastic slice governor with KV warmup crediting and SLO-steered preemption
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: continuous batching is efficient but tail latency and KV eviction storms happen under mixed workloads. We need a scheduler that enforces tenant SLOs while minimizing KV cold starts and GPU memory churn. Proposal: implement an Elastic Slice Governor (ESG) that issues short-lived 'slice credits' to tenants. Credits represent GPU micro-slice time and a KV warmup budget. Credits are earned/decayed based on recent SLO adherence and queue wait times. When under memory pressure ESG enables soft preemption where running slices are asked to yield after completing a safe token boundary; evicted KV segments are tracked and given a gradual warmup allowance to avoid immediate re-eviction. The system prefers to throttle new admissions over evicting hot KV pages for tenants within their SLO windows. Goals: reduce p99 latency SLO violations by 40% for P1 tenants, reduce KV eviction churn by 30%, and keep average GPU memory utilization above 80% without OOMs. Stages: 1) simulation with workload traces; 2) runtime prototype in batch scheduler; 3) canary on a dedicated pool; 4) full rollout with telemetry and automated rollback.
notes: Design summary and important trade-offs: 1) Soft vs hard preemption: prefer soft to avoid broken-inference responses and to allow graceful KV checkpointing. 2) Credit granularity: choose 50-200ms slices to balance latency and batching efficiency. 3) KV warmup credits: each credit can be spent to keep up to N KV pages pinned for M ms; this is a best-effort hint to the KV cache LRU/ageing system. 4) Admission control: when credits exhausted, requests are queued to a short-latency holdback with exponential backoff; if holdback exceeds threshold, they are diverted to a lower-cost model variant. 5) Fairness objective: SLO-weighted proportional fairness — tenants with stricter latency SLOs get higher burn-priority but are limited by a cap so bursty tenants cannot starve others. 6) Complexity: additional state per-tenant (credit balance, warmup reservations) will increase scheduler memory; we limit tracked tenants to top-200 active by default and garbage collect others. 7) Interaction with KV compaction: when compacting, temporarily boost warmup credits for tenants owning hot segments to reduce churn. 8) Rollback plan: revert to current proportional preemption and disable warmup hints if we see >5% increase in tail latency for golden synthetic tests.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation shows >= 30% reduction in KV eviction rate on mixed trace A
Canary (10% traffic) achieves <= 5% increase in cost/unit and reduces p99 SLO violations for P1 tenants by 35%
No increased incidence of application-level 5xx errors during canary
Telemetry dashboards for credit balance, KV warmup hit-rate, eviction rate, GPU mem headroom are onboarded
Automated rollback trigger implemented (p99 regression > 10% over baseline for 15m)
